
# Module 1: Tooling with uv {#mod-uv}

---

### uv: One Tool for the Python Workflow

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note}
### Replaces Many Legacy Tools
Consolidates `pip`, `pip-tools`, `pipx`, `poetry`, `pyenv`, `twine`, and `virtualenv` into a single fast CLI.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
### Blazing Fast (Written in Rust)
10–100x faster package installation and lock resolution. Drastically shortens CI pipeline runs.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
### Universal Lockfile (`uv.lock`)
Pins the entire dependency graph across platforms and Python versions for 100% reproducible environments.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note}
### Single-File Script Execution
PEP 723 inline dependency metadata allows single-file scripts to declare and isolate their own packages.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
### Manages Python Interpreters
Downloads, installs, and pins Python runtimes per project automatically without system packages.
:::

::: {.callout-important}
### Cargo-Style Workspaces
Native workspace support for modular multi-package monorepos and microservice agent collections.
:::
:::
:::

---

### The Project Lifecycle in Seven Commands

| Command | Operational Purpose |
| :--- | :--- |
| `uv init my-agent` | Create a new project with `pyproject.toml`, `.python-version`, and entry point |
| `uv add httpx pydantic` | Add runtime dependencies; automatically updates `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` |
| `uv remove httpx` | Remove a dependency cleanly from files and virtual environment |
| `uv sync` | Reconcile the local `.venv` to match `uv.lock` with surgical precision |
| `uv run pytest` | Run any command inside the virtual environment (auto-syncs environment first) |
| `uv lock --upgrade` | Re-resolve all dependencies and upgrade pinned package versions |
| `uv tree` | Inspect and visualize the full transitive dependency tree |

> **Golden Rule:** `.venv` and `uv.lock` are created automatically on first `uv add` or `uv run`. **You never activate the environment by hand.**

---

### Dependency Groups, CI and Production

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```bash
# Add development tools to dev group
uv add --dev pytest ruff pytest-asyncio

# Add documentation dependencies
uv add --group docs mkdocs

# Developer workstation: sync everything
uv sync

# CI environment: fail if lockfile changes
uv sync --frozen

# Production container: exclude test/lint tools
uv sync --no-dev

# Export for legacy platforms requiring requirements.txt
uv export --format requirements-txt > requirements.txt
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
#### Separation of Concerns
- **Dev vs Runtime:** Keep heavy linters, type checkers, and test runners out of production images.
- **Commit `uv.lock`:** Guarantee that every developer and every CI runner gets bit-for-bit identical packages.
- **Never Hand-Edit:** Always use `uv add` and `uv remove` so `pyproject.toml` and `uv.lock` stay strictly synchronized.
:::
:::

---

### Python Versions and Single-File Scripts

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```python
# /// script
# requires-python = ">=3.12"
# dependencies = [
#     "httpx>=0.27",
#     "rich",
# ]
# ///
import httpx
from rich import print

resp = httpx.get("https://httpbin.org/get")
print(f"[bold green]Status:[/bold green] {resp.status_code}")

# Run standalone:
# uv run example.py
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
#### PEP 723 Inline Metadata
- **Self-Contained Scripts:** No need to initialize a full project directory for one-off scrapers, evals, or benchmarks.
- **Isolated Cache:** `uv run` executes the script inside an isolated ephemeral cache, ignoring the surrounding project's dependencies.
- **Useful Commands:**
  - `uv init --script agent_eval.py`
  - `uv add --script agent_eval.py anthropic`
  - `uv run --with duckdb query.py`
:::
:::

### Tools: `uvx` and `uv tool`

| Command | Purpose | When to Use |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| `uvx ruff check .` | Run CLI tool in temporary environment | One-off checks, formatting PRs, quick audits |
| `uv tool install ruff` | Install CLI tool globally, isolated from system Python | Everyday tools you invoke across all terminal directories |
| `uv tool upgrade --all` | Upgrade all globally installed CLI tools | Routine developer workstation maintenance |
| `uv run --with pytest pytest` | Run command with ad-hoc package injected | Testing scripts without polluting `pyproject.toml` |

::: columns
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-note}
### Ruff
Extremely fast Python linter & formatter in Rust; replaces flake8, black, isort, bandit.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="33%"}
::: {.callout-tip}
### Type Checker
`mypy` or `pyright` for static safety checks in CI and editors.
:::
:::
::: {.column width="34%"}
::: {.callout-important}
### Pytest
The industry-standard test runner with fixture and async support.
:::
:::

### Anatomy of `pyproject.toml`

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```toml
[project]
name = "my-agent"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Autonomous Agent with LangGraph & ADK"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "pydantic>=2.7",
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
    "ruff>=0.4.0",
    "mypy>=1.10.0",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
#### Standard Sections (PEP 621)
- **`[project]`:**
  Defines package name, semver version, Python compatibility boundary, and core runtime requirements.
- **`[dependency-groups]`:**
  Standardized dev, test, and documentation groups (replaces legacy poetry extras).
- **`[tool.*]`:**
  Centralized configuration for developer tools (`ruff`, `pytest`, `mypy`), eliminating cluttered standalone config files.
:::
:::

---

### Project Layout that Scales

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
```
my-agent/
├── pyproject.toml        # Single source of truth
├── uv.lock               # Cross-platform deterministic lock
├── .python-version       # Pinned Python interpreter (e.g. 3.13)
├── .env                  # Environment secrets (NEVER commit!)
├── .gitignore            # Git exclusion rules
├── src/
│   └── my_agent/         # Primary package root
│       ├── __init__.py
│       ├── agent.py      # Core agent loop / state machine
│       ├── tools.py      # Exposed tools & schemas
│       ├── schemas.py    # Pydantic models
│       └── config.py     # Settings & env vars
└── tests/
    ├── conftest.py       # Global fixtures & mock models
    └── test_tools.py     # Unit tests mirroring src
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
#### Architectural Rules
1. **The `src` Layout:**
   Prevents accidental imports of un-built local directory code when running from repository root.
2. **Modular Micro-Components:**
   Split state schemas, tool implementations, configuration, and runtime graphs into distinct modules.
3. **Mirroring Tests:**
   Every module in `src/my_agent/<name>.py` corresponds to `tests/test_<name>.py`.
:::
:::

### Ruff: Lint and Format in One Pass

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```toml
# pyproject.toml configuration
[tool.ruff.lint]
select = [
    "E",     # pycodestyle errors
    "F",     # Pyflakes (unused vars/imports)
    "I",     # isort (import ordering)
    "UP",    # pyupgrade (modernize Python syntax)
    "B",     # flake8-bugbear (common bug traps)
    "ASYNC", # flake8-async (blocking calls in loops)
]
```

```bash
# Run linting with automated fix suggestions
uv run ruff check --fix

# Format entire codebase instantly
uv run ruff format
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
#### Essential Rule Sets for Agents
- **`I` (isort):** Ensures deterministic, clean import structures.
- **`UP` (pyupgrade):** Automatically updates older typing syntax to modern Python 3.12+ syntax (`int | None`).
- **`ASYNC`:** Catches catastrophic bugs in agent code, such as calling `time.sleep()` or `requests.get()` inside async functions.

> **Team Culture:** Let the formatter end style debates. Never disable a rule without an explicit `# noqa` comment explaining the engineering reason.
:::
:::

---

### Static Type Checking as a Habit

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-note}
### Pick a Checker
- **Mypy:** The established reference type checker.
- **Pyright:** Extremely fast, outstanding IDE integration.
- Choose one and configure it consistently across the entire team and CI.
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
### Ratchet Up Strictness
- Start lenient on legacy code (`basic` mode).
- Turn on strict checks (`disallow_untyped_defs`, `no_implicit_optional`) incrementally package by package.
:::
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
::: {.callout-important}
### Frameworks Reward Types
- LangGraph and ADK rely on type annotations to construct runtime state channels, state reducers, and JSON tool schemas.
- Invalid types cause runtime agent crashes mid-task.
:::

```bash
# Run type checker in CI pipeline
uv run mypy src
# or
uv run pyright src
```
:::
:::

### Git, Secrets, and Pre-Commit

::: columns
::: {.column width="50%"}
```gitignore
# Baseline .gitignore for Agent Projects
.venv/
.env
.env.*
__pycache__/
*.pyc
.pytest_cache/
.ruff_cache/
.mypy_cache/
dist/
*.sqlite3
```
:::

::: {.column width="50%"}
#### Secret Hygiene
- **Never Commit Credentials:** Store OpenAI/Anthropic API keys, database URLs, and bearer tokens exclusively in `.env` or system environment.
- **Automate with Pre-Commit:**
  Configure a local hook or git workflow to enforce `ruff check` and `ruff format` before commits are created.

::: {.callout-caution}
### Irreversible Exposure
A key committed once lives in Git commit history forever. If a secret leaks, rotate it immediately in the cloud provider console.
:::
:::
:::

### Lab 1: Build a Professional Project Skeleton

::: {.callout-tip}
#### Goal
Create a reproducible Python agent repository from scratch with linting, typing, and tests configured.
:::

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
1. Initialize project and pin Python 3.12 or later: `uv init my-agent && uv python pin 3.12`
2. Add runtime dependencies: `uv add httpx pydantic`
3. Add development dependencies: `uv add --dev pytest pytest-asyncio ruff mypy`
4. Configure `tool.ruff` and `tool.pytest.ini_options` in `pyproject.toml`
5. Write one passing unit test in `tests/test_basic.py`; execute with `uv run pytest`
6. Verify reproducibility: Delete `.venv` and rebuild completely via `uv sync`
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
#### Completion Criteria
- [x] A fresh checkout runs tests with a single `uv sync && uv run pytest`
- [x] `uv.lock` is tracked in git
- [x] `uv run ruff check` and `uv run ruff format --check` report 0 errors
- [x] **Stretch Goal:** Add a GitHub Actions CI workflow running `uv sync --frozen` and pytest.
:::
:::

### Lab 1: Complete Reference Implementation

::: columns
::: {.column width="55%"}
```toml
# pyproject.toml - Fully wired configuration
[project]
name = "my-agent"
version = "0.1.0"
description = "Autonomous Agent Core Skeleton"
readme = "README.md"
requires-python = ">=3.12"
dependencies = [
    "httpx>=0.27.0",
    "pydantic>=2.7.0",
]

[dependency-groups]
dev = [
    "pytest>=8.0.0",
    "pytest-asyncio>=0.23.0",
    "ruff>=0.4.0",
    "mypy>=1.10.0",
]

[tool.ruff]
line-length = 100

[tool.pytest.ini_options]
testpaths = ["tests"]
asyncio_mode = "auto"
```
:::

::: {.column width="45%"}
```python
# tests/test_skeleton.py
import pytest
from pydantic import BaseModel

class AgentStatus(BaseModel):
    name: str
    ready: bool

def test_project_wiring():
    status = AgentStatus(name="orchestrator", ready=True)
    assert status.name == "orchestrator"
    assert status.ready is True
```

```bash
# Execution & verification commands:
uv sync
uv run ruff check && uv run ruff format --check
uv run mypy src
uv run pytest
```
:::
:::
